finding.text: The runs page intro prints raw markdown: `**ask**`, `**outcome**`, `**0.5 means not sure**` and `[confidence.md](/framework/ext/Refine/md/doc/confidence/)` show as literal text, so the link to the scale can't be clicked (content: every mention a link; ask 4). Evidence: shots/…Refine-runs/1200.png, band 2. `p()` reads backticks only; use `b()`/`a()` for these.

On the new scale, 62% of the per-ask confidences (496 of 798) are still above 0.7, most at 0.8 or 0.85. Every one has an evidence string, so the rule holds. But this is the "lots of high numbers" pattern the owner disagreed with, and the spot-check found two outcome scores set high for fixes that are still open. Worth a calibration pass.

The days' input is mostly agent-written `requirements.md` briefs, not the owner's raw words, and 5 of the 7 days were capped at 20k characters. The readme says each day is a sample, but the runs page only says "(input capped)".

On the runs page each day is a wrapping paragraph of numbers and links. A small table (day · asks · ask · outcome · links) would read at a glance and stop the links breaking across lines at 1200 and 400. The page also builds rows with `document.createElement`/`innerHTML` instead of the framework's `p`/`a` tags.
The prompt-template part of ask 2 is covered by `Servex/ext/refine/ClarityScorer.js` (the only model prompt that asks for a score). `Server/refine.mjs` has no score prompt, so it needs no change.
